To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1D narrow graphene and h-BN nanofragments are characterized by strong spin polarization caused interface-induced structural asymmetries and indirect exchange interactions with the SrO-terminated LSMO(001).

1D narrow graphene- and hexagonal boron nitride zigzag nanoribbon are characterized by the spin polarization caused by the oxygen-mediated indirect exchange interaction with Mn ions of the LSMO support.

the spin polarization of 2D graphene and 2D h-BN nanofragments on a SrO surface of LSMO (001) surface is induced via indirect exchange interactions between π-conjugated states of fragments and d-states of Mn ions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms of spin polarization of 2D narrow zigzag graphene- and hBN nanoribbons and the nature of the interaction with the LSMO(100) surface.
the study of the electronic and spin structures of the 1D graphene- and h-boron nitride nanoribbons (NRs) on SrO-terminated LSMO(001), and their potential applications in spintronics.

the study of the structure of the interfaces, the mechanisms of the induced spin polarization, and the electronic structure of the 1D graphene- and hBN zigzag nanoribbon placed on a Sr-O terminated LSMO (001) surface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spin polarization of 2D nanofragments is induced by the asymmetry effect and the oxygen-mediated indirect exchange interaction with the substrate.
the spin polarization of the nanofragments can be controlled by their structural and electronic properties.

the DFT electronic structure calculations of 1D narrow graphene- and hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) nanoribbons on the SrO-terminated LSMO(001)-surface reveal that these systems can be used to design spintronic devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the spin-polarized electronic structure of 1D narrow graphene- and hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) nanoribbons on the SrO-terminated LSMO(001), as well as the nature of the interaction between them, is determined by the interface-induced structural asymmetries and oxygen-mediated indirect spin exchange interactions.
the results show a possibility for the design of LSMO-based heterosructures for spintronic nano devices, using one-atom thick graphene- or h-BN fragments.

the spin polarization of the graphene nanoribbon can be controlled by changing the width and the length of graphene nanoribbon, and the spin polarization of h-boron nitride nanoribbon can also be controlled by changing its length.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spin polarization of 2D materials on a SrO terminated LSMO(001)surface is possible and can be controlled by the nature of nanofragment.
it is possible to design a spintronic nanosystem based on a SrO terminated LSMO (001) surface with a 1D graphene- or h-BN zig-zag nanoribbon.
the spin polarization of the 1D narrow nanofragments can be induced by the interface interactions with a SrO- terminated LSMO(001).
